function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single individual—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed for millennia (e.g., static sparks, lightning). The systematic study and formalization of electrical concepts began with early experiments by people such as Thales of Miletus (observed static electricity), William Gilbert (named it “electricus”), and later, in the 17th–18th centuries, figures like Otto von Guericke, Stephen Gray, and especially Benjamin Franklin (who coined terms like “positive” and “negative”). In the 19th century, Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, and others built on their work to develop the laws of electromagnetism. Thus, electricity emerged from cumulative observations and experiments rather than a single discovery.
